reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / NCCN & genetics references
clinicalPearls: Caused by germline variants in the VHL tumour suppressor gene, inherited autosomal dominantly with high penetrance and a substantial de novo rate
Hallmark lesions are haemangioblastomas of the retina and central nervous system, especially the cerebellum, brainstem, and spinal cord
Retinal haemangioblastomas can be detected early by fundoscopy and treated to prevent visual loss, making regular ophthalmic surveillance essential
Clear cell renal cell carcinoma and renal cysts are common and are a leading cause of cancer death, so renal imaging surveillance is central to management
Phaeochromocytomas and paragangliomas occur and must be excluded biochemically before any surgery or during pregnancy to avoid catastrophic hypertensive crises
Other features include pancreatic cysts and neuroendocrine tumours, endolymphatic sac tumours causing hearing loss, and epididymal or broad ligament cystadenomas
Surveillance is lifelong and multi-organ, combining periodic imaging of the brain, spine, abdomen, and eyes with biochemical screening for catecholamine excess
Nephron-sparing surgery is favoured for renal tumours to preserve renal function given the high risk of new and bilateral tumours
reference.pathophysiology: The VHL protein is part of a complex that targets hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) for degradation under normal oxygen conditions. Loss of VHL function leads to constitutive HIF accumulation as if the tissue were hypoxic, driving overexpression of vascular endothelial growth factor and other proangiogenic and growth factors. This produces the highly vascular haemangioblastomas and promotes the development of clear cell renal carcinoma and the other characteristic tumours through inappropriate angiogenesis and cell proliferation.
additionalDifferentials: Hereditary papillary or other familial renal cell carcinoma syndromes
Sporadic haemangioblastoma or renal cell carcinoma
additionalInvestigations: Germline VHL sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis with genetic counselling
MRI of the brain and spine for haemangioblastoma surveillance
Abdominal imaging (MRI, CT, or ultrasound) for renal, pancreatic, and adrenal lesions
Dilated retinal examination for retinal haemangioblastomas
Plasma or urinary metanephrines to screen for phaeochromocytoma/paraganglioma, with audiological assessment for endolymphatic sac tumours
redFlags: Unrecognised phaeochromocytoma precipitating a hypertensive crisis under anaesthesia or in pregnancy
Enlarging or symptomatic central nervous system haemangioblastoma causing raised intracranial pressure or cord compression
Growing renal mass exceeding the threshold for intervention with metastatic potential
New visual, neurological, or hearing symptoms in a known gene carrier
reference.prognosis: With lifelong surveillance and timely intervention, many complications are preventable and life expectancy is substantially improved, but renal cell carcinoma and central nervous system disease remain the principal causes of death. Outcome depends heavily on adherence to multi-organ screening and on nephron-sparing, function-preserving management.
pitfalls: Operating on a patient without first excluding phaeochromocytoma, risking a hypertensive crisis
Performing radical rather than nephron-sparing surgery and hastening renal failure given recurrent bilateral tumours
Attributing hearing loss to common causes and missing an endolymphatic sac tumour
Lapses in the lifelong multi-organ surveillance schedule allowing tumours to present late
management: Offer the HIF-2-alpha inhibitor belzutifan for VHL-associated renal cell carcinoma, central nervous system haemangioblastomas and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours not requiring immediate surgery
Manage renal cell carcinoma with nephron-sparing partial nephrectomy or ablation, and keep small renal lesions under active surveillance to preserve renal function
Treat retinal haemangioblastomas early with laser photocoagulation, cryotherapy or anti-VEGF agents to prevent visual loss
Resect or use stereotactic radiosurgery for symptomatic or enlarging central nervous system haemangioblastomas
Screen biochemically for phaeochromocytoma with plasma or urinary metanephrines and give alpha-adrenergic blockade before any surgery or pregnancy to avert hypertensive crisis
Coordinate lifelong multi-organ surveillance including brain and spine MRI, abdominal imaging, dilated retinal examination and audiology through a specialist multidisciplinary team
Provide genetic counselling and cascade testing of at-risk relatives given autosomal dominant inheritance
